title: A file that doubled in size
oneLine: A permissions change made a bot detection file double in size, every server loaded it, and the proxy crashed on the extra features.

sources.title: Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025 | Cloudflare Blog

facts.label: Feature limit
facts.quote: Currently that limit is set to 200, well above our current use of ~60 features.

facts.label: File growth
facts.quote: That feature file, in turn, doubled in size.

facts.label: Regenerated
facts.quote: the file was being generated every five minutes

facts.label: Core traffic
facts.quote: the majority of core traffic to stop flowing through our network

facts.label: Everything normal
facts.quote: As of 17:06 all systems at Cloudflare were functioning as normal.

events.label: Bad file reaches the edge
events.quote: Deployment reaches customer environments, first errors observed on customer HTTP traffic.

events.label: First automated alert
events.quote: The first automated test detected the issue at 11:31

events.label: Incident call
events.quote: The incident call was created at 11:35.

events.label: Feature file suspected
events.quote: We were confident that the Bot Management configuration file was the trigger for the incident.

events.label: New files stopped
events.quote: Stopped creation and propagation of new Bot Management configuration files.

events.label: Core traffic back
events.quote: Core traffic was largely flowing as normal by 14:30.

levers.label: Rollout
levers.why: The regenerated file went straight to every machine
levers.quote: The larger-than-expected feature file was then propagated to all the machines that make up our network.

levers.label: File ingestion
levers.why: The proxy trusted its own generated file and crashed when it broke the limit
levers.quote: Hardening ingestion of Cloudflare-generated configuration files in the same way we would for user-generated input

levers.label: Alert to stop
levers.why: Good and bad files flapping every few minutes first looked like an attack
levers.quote: Enabling more global kill switches for features

afterwards.quote: Hardening ingestion of Cloudflare-generated configuration files in the same way we would for user-generated input
Enabling more global kill switches for features
Eliminating the ability for core dumps or other error reports to overwhelm system resources
Reviewing failure modes for error conditions across all core proxy modules

assumptions.what: The bad file stays on every server from 11:28 until new files stop
assumptions.why: In reality good and bad files alternated every five minutes until every node produced the bad one. The postmortem does not say when that settled.

assumptions.what: A hit server still serves 25% of its traffic
assumptions.why: The postmortem gives no number for how much traffic was lost.

assumptions.what: Service comes back with a 128 second time constant once the change is pulled
assumptions.why: Fitted so the replay is back by 14:30, as the postmortem reports.

assumptions.what: The change reaches every server within a few seconds
assumptions.why: The postmortem does not say how fast it spread.

assumptions.what: Each staged rollout step waits 10 minutes, and early stages carry 1 to 2% of traffic each
assumptions.why: Used only when you switch the rollout to staged. The postmortem does not describe a staged path.
